findings.location: Several instances: Psalm 1 quote and surrounding sentence "near the rivers of water"
findings.source_quote: "And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season..." (Psalms 1:3)
findings.suggested_fix: Use a more natural and standard French idiom for 'rivers of water' and correct the plural/grammar. Replace "près des courants d’eaux" with "près des cours d'eau" or "au bord des cours d'eau" so the phrase reads smoothly and idiomatically while preserving meaning. E.g. change the sentence fragment to: «...comme un arbre planté au bord des cours d'eau, qui donne son fruit en sa saison...»
findings.translation_quote: « Et il sera comme un arbre planté près des courants d’eaux, qui donne son fruit en sa saison ; ... » (Psaumes 1:3).

findings.source_quote: English uses generic 'you' throughout (e.g. "Can I have...", "Does He feel cold and distant to you?", "If you are struggling...")
findings.suggested_fix: Make the target-language second-person usage consistent. Either render the whole article in the formal/plural 'vous' or in the informal singular 'tu'. Many opening paragraphs and headings use 'vous' (formal), then most pastoral/disciplinary sections switch to 'tu' (informal). Choose one register and apply it consistently across all paragraphs, preserving original HTML. Example: if keeping 'tu', change earlier occurrences of 'vous' to 'tu' (and corresponding verb forms); if keeping 'vous', change the informal 'tu' forms later to 'vous'.
findings.translation_quote: Mixed usage: early text uses 'votre', 'vous' (e.g. "votre relation avec Dieu", "Est-ce qu’il vous semble froid et distant..."), later text uses 'tu' and 'ton' (e.g. "Tu ne dois jamais penser...", "Ouvrir ton cœur...").
